title: Bulk Slash
subtitle: A machine with two ways to fight
summary: Bulk Slash is CAProduction's transforming-mech action game, released by Hudson Soft for Saturn in Japan on 11 July 1997.
body: Bulk Slash is CAProduction's transforming-mech action game, released by Hudson Soft for Saturn in Japan on 11 July 1997. Pilot Cress Dawley fights a futuristic war across seven stages, switching his machine between ground combat and flight. Missions give the player objectives to pursue before confronting a boss. The transformation makes the environment useful in two different ways: a place to maneuver and fight on foot becomes airspace to cross, with weapons and movement changing alongside the machine's shape.

Hidden navigators can be found during the stages and recruited through the Manageable Intelligent Support System, abbreviated M.I.S.S. Each brings particular support abilities, and the selected companion gains experience separately from the player's score. Returning with that navigator develops the relationship and can alter the ending. The player therefore has another reason to explore a stage beyond its immediate military objective. Between missions, choosing a companion becomes part of preparing the next sortie, connecting the action to a growing supporting cast.

CAProduction had previously worked on Hagane and Sapphire, bringing experience in fast action to Saturn's three-dimensional spaces. Takeshi Sato composed the soundtrack. The game remained a Japanese release, with an English fan translation arriving in 2021. Its identity rests on the connection between a freely moving combat machine and the navigator beside its pilot. Learning a mission means understanding which form works best in a space, while further visits can uncover another companion and another reason to follow the route again.
